Based on the analysis performed on your uploaded DEM file, here are the results:

## Results

**1. Mean slope of dem.tif: 6.01°**

The slope was computed using Horn's algorithm (the standard GIS 3×3-window method), calculated in meters since the DEM is in UTM 16N (EPSG:32616) at 30 m resolution. The mean slope is **6.01 degrees** (median 5.76°, std 0.80°). This indicates gentle terrain — the DEM spans 200–497 m elevation over a 4.5 km × 6.0 km area.

**2. Watershed area draining to the outlet: 16.2 km²**

The watershed was delineated using D8 flow direction + flow accumulation, tracing upstream from the outlet at UTM x=392265, y=4434015 (which maps to the DEM's minimum-elevation cell, 200.3 m, on the southern edge). The contributing area is **18,000 of the 30,000 cells**, giving:

- **Area = 18,000 cells × (30 m)² = 16,200,000 m² = 16.2 km²**

The watershed polygon is on your interactive map (reprojected to WGS84), and the outlet at 40.0495°N, 88.2630°W falls within its bounds, confirming correct placement.

- Watershed polygon (GeoJSON, on map): [file_bc5100a40d4f](https://agent/files/file_bc5100a40d4f/download)
- Summary text: [dem_analysis_results.txt](https://agent/files/file_66d699b41a49/download)

**One caveat on the watershed:** the outlet lies at the DEM's lowest point on the southern edge, so the contributing area is bounded by the DEM extent itself — the true watershed may extend beyond this 30 m tile if the DEM is a clipped subset of a larger terrain. Within the provided DEM, the answer is 16.2 km².
